questions.stem: A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed $v_0$ and an angle $\theta$. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?

options.explanation: The speed at maximum height involves horizontal velocity, which is $v_0 \cos \theta$.
At maximum height, the vertical component of velocity is zero, leaving only horizontal $v_0 \cos \theta$.
$v_0 \sin \theta$ is the initial vertical velocity, which becomes zero at the maximum height.
The horizontal component of velocity remains unchanged at maximum height unless acted upon by external forces.

2.  A spaceship is traveling with an initial velocity of 𝑣⃗ = (20.1 𝑚/𝑠)𝑖̂ when its rockets 
0
fire, imparting an acceleration of 𝑎⃗ = (2.02𝑚⁄𝑠2)𝑖̂+(4.03𝑚⁄𝑠2)𝑗̂. Based on this 
scenario, which of the following statements is correct? 
A.  The x-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant. 
B.  The y-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant. 
C. Both the direction of motion and speed change. 
D.  None of the above is correct.
questions.stem: A spaceship is traveling with an initial velocity $\vec{v}_0 = (20.1 \text{ m/s})\hat{i}$ when its rockets fire, imparting an acceleration of $\vec{a} = (2.02\text{ m/s}^2)\hat{i} + (4.03\text{ m/s}^2)\hat{j}$. Based on this scenario, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The x-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant.
options.explanation: Since there is an acceleration component in the $\hat{i}$ direction, the x-velocity changes.

options.text: The y-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant.
options.explanation: The y-velocity changes because there is an acceleration component in the $\hat{j}$ direction.

options.text: Both the direction of motion and speed change.
options.explanation: With both $x$ and $y$ accelerations, the speed and direction change.

options.text: None of the above is correct.
options.explanation: Option C is correct as both speed and direction change due to the acceleration.
